links.note: Valli's age - eight. 24209 is the premise, an eight-year-old making her first bus journey.
Valli aged eight - the premise of the story.
Valli's full name, Valliammai - the girl the premise of 24209 turns on.
What Valli did one fine spring day - caught the bus to the town. The first journey of 24209.
Valli catching the bus to town one spring day - the journey the story is built on.
What two things Valli ought to take travelling alone for the first time - an eight-year-old's first journey out, which is 24209.
Valli's favourite pastime - watching the street outside. 24212 is her curiosity and keen watching.
Standing at the front doorway watching the street - the curiosity of 24212.
Valli's favourite pastime and unending source of joy - watching the street. Her curiosity about things.
What was an unending source of joy for Valli - watching the street outside, which is the curiosity in 24212.
An eight-year-old very curious about things and her favourite pastime - 24212's wording.
What was a source of unending joy for Valli - watching children and the street. Her curiosity.
The most fascinating scene in the street - the bus with a new set of passengers every time. Her keen watching.
The most fascinating thing Valli saw on the street - the bus and its changing passengers, which she watched closely.
How many times the bus crossed her street each hour - twice. A detail she learnt by listening, which is 24216.
The bus crossing her street twice an hour - one of the details she picked up.
How she picked up the details of the bus journey - by listening carefully to conversations. That is 24216.
How she learnt the details of the journey - listening to neighbours and regular passengers.
The town six miles from the village - one of the facts she learnt about the trip.
The meaning of 'wistfully' - longingly, as she stared at people getting on and off the bus. The wish she held to, in 24213.
'Wistfully' as longingly - her persistent wish for a bus ride.
Her overwhelming desire - to travel by bus. 24213 is that wish held to.
Riding on the bus as her single wish - the determination of 24213.
What made Valli jealous - hearing friends' stories of bus journeys, which fed her own resolve.
'A tiny wish crept into her head and grew there' - the wish developing over time and being held to, which is 24213.
Why Valli stood up - she could not see out properly. The view she came for, which is 24218.
Valli standing up because she could not see out - her appetite for the view.
Why Valli stands on the seat and what she sees - the canal, the palm trees, the distant mountains. 24218 lists these.
The train looking like a speck in the distance - part of the view that delights her.
Valli clapping her hands with delight - her joy at what she saw from the window.
Valli absorbing the natural beauty and clapping at the running cow - the delight in the view of 24218.
What the old man said that annoyed her - he merely asked her to sit, treating her as a child. Her self-respect in 24214.
The old man asking her to sit, which she resented as condescension.
The old man's remark that annoyed her - being told to sit like a child. 24214's refusal of pity.
Why the old lady asked Valli so many questions - she was concerned about her, which Valli resented. Her insistence on being treated properly.
The old lady's questions out of concern - the pity Valli refuses in 24214.
Why Valli found the woman repulsive - her betel-chewing mouth and her prying. 24214's refusal of unwanted attention.
Why Valli would not make friends with the elderly woman - she disliked her and resented being pitied.
Why Valli would not talk to the elderly woman - she would not be treated as a child needing care.
The meaning of 'repulsive' - causing strong dislike, used of the woman whose concern Valli rejects.
